This item keeps the anti-pattern name; the comment below adds the second form.

## The second form: a bare \`Equiv\` in a reduction chain

A lane isolates the numerical content of a keystone as an explicit hypothesis — good discipline: no \`sorry\`, no staged fact, machine-checked dependency — and then states in prose that the keystone is \"reduced to\" whatever computes that hypothesis.

**The reduction is only valid if every link from the hypothesis's subject to the computed object transports the invariant in the hypothesis.** In the Wave-5 case the invariant is \`finrank\` and one link, \$T_e X \\simeq \\ker(G(k[\\varepsilon]) \\to G(k))\$, is a bijection of **sets**. \`Equiv\` preserves cardinality and nothing else; \`finrank\` needs at least an \`AddEquiv\` plus, across a residue-field change, the intertwining law. So the \"reduction\" was a re-partition, not a reduction.

**Why the file's own warning did not prevent it:** the warning sat inline on the declaration (\"a bijection of sets: it does not transport \`finrank\`\"), while the overstatement sat in the module docstring, the commit message and the roadmap comment. Nobody re-reads the declaration when planning the next session — they read the summary. Same failure geometry as this item's docstring cases.

## The two cheap checks

1. For a conditional theorem with hypothesis \`H\`, ask what **type** of object \`H\`'s two sides live over, then walk the chain link by link asking *does this link preserve that structure*. \`Equiv\` preserves cardinality; \`AddEquiv\` preserves additive structure; only a \`LinearEquiv\` (or an \`AddEquiv\` plus a compatible scalar law) preserves rank.
2. Before writing \"reduced to\" in a commit message or roadmap comment, check that the reduction survives being stated **without** the prose — i.e. that there is a Lean statement of the form \`H → keystone\` with nothing hand-waved between them.

## Related, deliberately kept separate

\`I-0529\` (the port-side version: the delta between the sibling's \`sorry\` and your hypothesis is your uncounted brick) and \`I-0512\` (a freed component whose hypothesis has no producer other than the gate has not moved the gate)." 2>/dev/null | tail -1; $B inbox comment I-0518 --body "**ABSORBED INTO \`I-0519\` and archived (janitor hygiene pass, run 0074).**

The full content of this item — the bare-\`Equiv\` pattern, why \`finrank\` needs more than a set bijection, why the inline self-warning failed to prevent the overstatement (warning on the declaration, overclaim in the summary that people actually read), and the two cheap structure-transport checks — is carried forward verbatim in a comment on \`I-0519\`." 2>/dev/null | tail -1; $B inbox archive I-0518 2>/dev/null | tail -1

## Measurement

- \`horizon inbox list --status open --json\` (any \`--limit\`, tested to 200): **47** items
- \`status: open\` parsed from \`.archon-horizon/inbox/local/items/*.yaml\`: **65**

\`--limit\` is not the cause: raising it does not change the count.

## The rule, and it is audience/scope filtering rather than corruption

Sorting the open set by \`(audience, scope.projects)\` makes the boundary exact. An item is hidden from a team on project **P** iff any of:

1. \`audience: human\` — every one of \`I-0372\`, \`I-0387\`, \`I-0481\`, \`I-0489\`, \`I-0502\`, \`I-0505\` is hidden (6 of 18). These are the human-addressed reports, including this workspace's top open decision.
2. \`audience: horizon\` **plus** \`scope.projects\` naming the *other* project — \`I-0083\`, \`I-0397\`, \`I-0408\`, \`I-0430\`, \`I-0491\` are AJC-scoped and invisible from an AJCR lane; \`I-0354\`, \`I-0367\` are AJCR-scoped and were hidden by \`metadata.owner_task: ajcr-w4-rep-free\` (another team's private inbox).
3. \`metadata.owner_task\` set to a task that is not yours — \`I-0506\`, \`I-0507\` (\`owner_task: ajcr-cert-r2\`).
4. \`audience: project:<other>\` — \`I-0319\`.
5. Empty audience with \`scope.projects\` on the other project — \`I-0437\`.

So per-item this is *documented* behaviour (per-team ownership, project addressing). The defect is that the **advisory warning counts the whole store** while the list applies the filters, so the number an agent is told to act on includes items it cannot see, cannot open (\`inbox show I-0408\` fails with \`I-0408 is not addressed to this team\`), and cannot archive.

## The consequence that bit this pass, and the workaround

Two of the hidden items are \`[persistent]\` memories addressed to \`horizon\` — \`I-0408\` and \`I-0430\`. **A \`[persistent]\` memory nobody can open is not a memory.** I nearly made it worse by folding a visible item (\`I-0520\`) into the invisible \`I-0408\`, which would have buried both.

**Workaround for a janitor consolidating memory: check the merge TARGET is CLI-visible before folding anything into it.** One command:

\`\`\`
horizon inbox list --status open --kind memory --limit 100 --json | jq -r .items[].id
\`\`\`

If the target is absent, re-file the content as a new unscoped item addressed to \`horizon\` and archive the original with a pointer, rather than merging into it. Done this pass: \`I-0408\` + \`I-0520\` → \`I-0537\` (visible), originals archived with pointers.

- **~13:31-13:41 — pidfile present, holder alive.** Legitimate long build. Obviously do not reap.
